Enter the Hybrid

While pure electric cars rely entirely on a battery, hybrid cars combine a combustion engine with an electric motor — the range of conventional fuel with the efficiency of electric power. Six parts make it work.

1D–4D · Data → Drawing → Geometry → Time

Closing the Loop

For over a century, automotive engineering ran an open loop: energy extracted, burned for momentary movement, and permanently lost as heat. Hybrid mechanics close it.

The Open Loop — Conventional

Fuel→ Mechanical Motion→ Heat Waste

The Semi-Closed Loop — Hybrid

Fuel / Plug-in→ Motion→ Regenerative Braking→ Electricity→ back to Fuel/Plug-in node
